content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Lexington

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a specific combination of education and project-management experience. Review PMI's eligibility criteria—typically a secondary degree plus years of directed project work, or a four-year degree plus fewer years of experience. Verify you meet these thresholds before investing in training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Attend all sessions synchronously from anywhere, interact with active certified practitioners, and cover the full PMBOK Guide framework. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement for PMP eligibility.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing Granite PM Academy's bootcamp, submit your official PMI PMP application. Document your education, project experience, and training completion. Pay the PMI exam fee to schedule your computer-based exam at an authorized testing center.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor feedback—to solidify your readiness. Schedule your computer-based PMP exam at a local Lexington testing facility. Plan to sit for the four-hour, multiple-choice assessment.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP is valid for three years. During each renewal cycle, earn professional development units through PMI-approved activities—training, conferences, volunteering, or publishing. Renew before expiration to keep your credential active and demonstrate ongoing commitment to project-management excellence.
